of: A mechanism by which a previously available course of action becomes unexercisable without its holder declining it and without any party at the holder's own table deciding about it, named with the condition lost (a permission, a capability, a counterparty, a coordination), the carrier that runs the clock, and the last intervention that could have kept it, and sorted by what the clock is made of, from clocks the holder never started to clocks the holder's own care for the option started: a closure that must strike before it can be known, a date on someone else's docket, a date on the option's parent, the holder's own development, the record's last witness, the world healing faster than the forum, a ratifier's term, a counterparty's transfer or planning cycle, a coordination's half-life, the holder's own growth, then the act that vests, the exercise that keeps, the readiness that spoils, the move on a neighbouring matter, the new state's first act, the machine that holds the option open, and the pause paper whose renewal belongs to the adversary.
map_register: Operator-grade and concrete: bank holidays and Sunday decrees, bar dates and opt-out postcards, emergency authorizations, eye patches, last-known-well times, mootness and class certification, adjournment sine die, memoranda of lease, reorganizations that absorb a vacancy, sixty-day signatures, approval ceilings, poured footings, empty flights and irrigated fields, thawed vials, first responsive pleadings, first writes, ECMO circuits and mine pumps, tolling agreements; drawn from capital controls, bankruptcy, public-health law, paediatrics, stroke care, constitutional litigation, legislatures, real property, employment, recall elections, mergers, land use, aviation and water law, cold-chain logistics, patent and civil procedure, software migration, transplant medicine, and litigation practice.

items.out: You notice the address is scheduled for Sunday. Nothing is said about the banks, and that is the sign, because a closure of this kind is only a closure if nobody is told; told, it would be the starting gun. So the doors will shut in the hours you cannot reach them, the Friday night, the holiday the calendar already had, and the announcement, when it comes, will describe a thing that has already happened. Greece in June 2015 heard a Sunday speech and did not find the banks open on Monday the 29th. Cyprus in March 2013 was given a bank holiday and watched it lengthen, day by day, while parliament refused the first levy, and the holiday ended only when the bail-in had become law. Argentina was told on a Saturday in December 2001. The export licence is suspended and the delisting is published after the fact, in the same tense. What is going is a permission, the leave to move what is yours. What runs the clock is the authority's calendar, and the calendar is laid against your locked hours on purpose. The only move that would have kept it was made on rumour, weeks ago, at the price of being wrong and at the discount the rumour market charges, and the money that left Greece that spring left on nothing firmer than that. Hold onto this: of every expiry on this map, this is the one whose notice cannot come first. A holder who waits for a date is waiting for a thing the mechanism forbids. The small signs are all there is. The deposit counted as owned and unreachable behind glass on a Friday, runway-illusions' Cash behind glass, is this same thing seen from the far side; what you are reading here is what chose the Friday. It is not investor-tells' Let it lapse, a fuse you can test by letting it pass, since anything that can be probed is not this, which must be a surprise or is nothing. And it is not an offer withdrawn or a rival's foreclosure, which somebody at your own table decides, since this is a rule on a class and nobody at your table was asked. Keep it on that fence, and not on any claim that the exit dies as a side effect of something else: the decree names the exit and forbids it.

The postcard looks like advertising. That is the first sign, and it is built to be missed: the settlement's opt-out date is printed on it, and the printing is enough. Somewhere a proceeding you are not attending has fixed a date, and the law has already decided that you have read it. The bankruptcy court sets a bar date for proofs of claim and notices it, for the creditors the debtor could not name, by publication. The probate creditor's window opens the day the notice runs in the county paper and closes on schedule. What goes is a permission, the standing to be paid or to sue on your own account. What runs the clock is the bar-date order together with the rule of constructive notice, under which a line in a newspaper counts as your knowledge. The move that would have kept it is a one-page proof of claim, a signed opt-out, the cheapest filing in the law and the one least often made, because the person who would make it is, by the construction of the thing, the person who was not told. So read the mail you are about to throw away, and read the legal notices, because the date is on someone else's docket and it is being written against you. Runway-illusions' Stamp's clock is the near case, a permission with a date you can read on the stamp; this is the date written elsewhere and imputed to you. It is not deal-deaths' Missing witness: the record is complete, and nothing is missing from it but you from the room.

The grant you hold has no date on it. Look for the sign elsewhere: the paper it was issued under has one. The emergency-use authorization does not end on its own merits; it ends when the declaration it was issued under is terminated, and that is a different paper from the public-health emergency that ended in May 2023 and left the authorizations standing, the kind of distinction you learn by watching the wrong paper. The cross-state telehealth licence went with each state's emergency, in 2021 and 2022, one state at a time. The wartime power, the pilot programme run under a waiver, the sub-lease under a head lease: each is quiet in itself and ends when its parent does. What goes is a permission. What runs the clock is the parent instrument's date, which you never signed and may never have read, and the first thing you must do is find which paper is the parent, since the one you read had no date to find. The move that would have kept it is conversion, a full approval, a permanent rule, a licence in your own name, filed while the parent still stands, and conversion is slow enough that it must be begun while the emergency looks endless, which is precisely when nobody begins it. The stillness of the emergency is the sign. This is not Bar date in the newspaper, where the date sits on a docket and is imputed to you; here the date is honest, only it is on a different paper from your option. And it is not lead-time-floors' Calendar with nothing in it, a wait the rule imposes; this rule does not wait, it ends.

A squint, glanced at and forgotten. The child does not know there is an eye to save, and could not, because the clock here is the child's own development, running on a schedule the child cannot read and nobody can read exactly. Amblyopia is most correctable by patching the good eye in the first years; after about seven it responds less, and less completely, though the trials of the 2000s found response into the early teens, so the edge is soft and it is still an edge. The clubfoot is cast in infancy. The second language spoken without an accent is claimed as a window and disputed as a hard one. The duckling imprints on its first day. What goes is a capability, the cortex's willingness to rewire. What runs the clock is the developmental timetable. And because the holder is a child, the last intervention is necessarily in another hand: the preschool vision check, the parent who looks twice at the squint. The option belongs to one person and its keeping to another, and where no screening programme exists the option expires unseen, at a rate that is a property of the programme and not of any child. So the sign to read is not in the child. It is in whether anybody is looking. This sits beside Last known well, where a witness dates the option; here the holder cannot be its own witness at all. It is not a use-it-or-lose-it, since nothing the child does or leaves undone moves the clock.

She went to bed well. That is the last thing anyone can swear to, and in the morning it is the only fact the protocol will accept. The stroke that happened somewhere in the night is dated not by the artery but by the last witness, so the four-and-a-half-hour window for thrombolysis is counted from bedtime, and the wake-up stroke has lost the drug no matter when the vessel closed. The same rule governs the opened vial with no time written on the label and the sample whose chain of custody has a gap: each is treated as expired at the earliest hour it could have been. What goes is a capability, a treatment the protocol now forbids. What runs the clock is the protocol's timestamp rule, which asks for a witness and not for the tissue. The move that would have kept it is a witness, someone awake, a time written on the vial, or a witness of a different kind, the imaging that reads the tissue's own clock, which is how the WAKE-UP trial of 2018 gave the drug back to patients with no seen onset. So watch for the gap in the record before you watch for the harm. The body may still allow what the paper no longer will. This belongs beside witness-architectures, which asks what must exist for a trace to form: here is the option that dies for want of a trace while the fact would still permit it. It is not Patch before seven, where the body's own clock has run; here the body's clock may not have run, and the record's has.

Look at the calendar of the court and then at the calendar of the harm. When the second is shorter, the sign is already there. The student who challenged the law school's admissions was about to graduate, and the case was dismissed as moot (DeFunis, 1974); nobody declined him and nobody ruled. The pregnancy is over before the appeal. The election is held before the ballot-access case. The tenant is out before the housing court sits. The employee's grievance dissolves with the reorganization that abolished the post. What goes is a permission, the justiciability of the claim. What runs the clock is the ratio of the forum's pace to the harm's duration, a number no one at the table sets. The move that would have kept it is a structure that outlives the one harm: the class certified before the named plaintiff's harm ends, which Sosna (1975) allowed, or the doctrine that a harm capable of repetition yet evading review may be decided anyway, on which Roe rested. So the option is kept by a coordination or by a rule, and never by hurrying. Hurrying is the reflex, and it is the wrong reading of the sign. This is not deal-deaths' Cost of the last mile, where a surplus is eaten along a curve, since nothing is eaten here; the harm is simply over. And it is not Bar date in the newspaper, since there is no date anywhere to have missed.

The bill is on the calendar and the calendar is running out. Nobody has spoken against it; that is what should make you look. The body that could have said yes is nearing the end of its own term with the matter still pending, and the body that follows it will never have to say no, because it starts from nothing. Bills die on adjournment sine die by the thousand, each session, without a recorded no, and must be reintroduced from the beginning. The treaty is signed and waits for a parliament that is dissolved. The permit application is before a council that is re-elected. The old board agreed in the hallway and had not minuted it when the board was reconstituted at the meeting. The committee that approved the offer is disbanded in the reorganization. What expires is the matter's place in the process, since the successor starts it at zero. What goes is a counterparty, the specific body whose yes was available. What runs the clock is the ratifier's own calendar, its election, its session, its term. The move that would have kept it is the vote scheduled before adjournment, the carry-over motion, the approval minuted rather than agreed in the hallway. The treaty cases are simplified, since most unratified treaties were in the end refused by someone; the clean form is the bill. This sits beside deal-deaths' Ratifier's other deal, where the ratifier wanted a different bargain; here the ratifier wanted this one and was gone before the vote. It is not Landlord changes, where the counterparty is replaced by a transfer; here it is replaced by the calendar.

The for-sale sign goes up on the building. The renewal you were promised is not in the lease; it was said, across a desk, by the man who is now selling. A buyer takes the title, and the title does not carry unrecorded promises, so the buyer takes free of yours. The manager who said 'we'll take you back' has given notice. The side letter with the fund's partner is one the fund's successor manager has never seen. The supplier's verbal priority leaves with the account executive. An option held in a person rather than on the paper that transfers expires at the counterparty's next transfer, which you do not control and often do not see coming until the sign is on the lawn. What goes is a counterparty, the one whose word held the option. What runs the clock is the register, the deed, the fund agreement, the offer letter on letterhead, the paper on which the option was never written. The move that would have kept it was recording: a memorandum of option on the title, a side letter countersigned by the entity, the promise put on the paper that binds successors, at the cost of the awkwardness of asking a friendly counterparty to bind their unknown replacement. That awkwardness was the thing to read; it is the sign that the promise lives in a person. Term-sheet-powers' Successor in the chair is the mirror, where the replacement exercises a term the friend would not have; here the replacement declines to honour a term the friend gave. It is not Chair grown over, where the counterparty stays and the shape goes.

Nobody has asked when you are coming back. Take that as the sign. The leave was taken with no return date, and the post has not been refused to you; it has simply been split among three people at the reorganization, the way a budget line is reallocated at year end, the way the supplier's line is retooled for the customer who stayed, the way the co-founder's seat stops being left empty at the next hire. The option to return rests on a vacancy the counterparty has not yet re-planned, and it expires at the next planning cycle without anyone deciding against you. What expires is the return to the seat; employment there afterwards is a new negotiation, from outside. What goes is a capability on the counterparty's side, the shape that could receive you. What runs the clock is the counterparty's planning cadence, quarterly, annual, the next reorganization, and it sets the date without reference to you at all. The move that would have kept it is a dated return, a leave rather than a resignation, a reservation the cycle must respect, or the return itself before the cycle turns. So when the quarter is closing and no one has mentioned your chair, that silence is the whole of the warning. Traces-of-the-unlived's Vacancy tenant is the case where preparing for a future breeds its opponents; here nobody opposes the return, the absence is simply absorbed. It is not forms-of-return's Reentry burn, a road open and hostile one way; this road has closed.

The first signatures are already older than the last ones, and the oldest are about to stop counting. An option that needs many simultaneous yeses is not lost all at once; it goes one yes at a time, from the back, and the gathering has to outrun the decay or the whole thing sours. Michigan invalidates recall signatures older than sixty days; California requires all of them to fall within a hundred and sixty. The tender offer's minimum condition must be met by the offer's expiry. The crowd in the square goes home. The reunion becomes impossible one death at a time. What goes is a coordination. What runs the clock is the validity window on each act of assent, written by the rule or by the assenter's own attention. The move that would have kept it is a gathering rate, paid circulators, a date agreed in advance, a pact that binds the early yeses until the last one arrives. The recall and tender cases are observed; the crowd is an analogy. So the sign is in the dates on the earliest sheets, and you read them against the pace of the newest. Who-can-be-bound's Place in line is an ordering lost by your leaving; this is the coordination lost by others' leaving. It is not Session ends, where one body's calendar kills the matter; here many small calendars do.

Each round is a celebration, and each round moves the price a little further past a number nobody in the room has checked: the largest deal any of your three strategic buyers has ever done. Your preference stack is already past it. Your own growth is carrying the counterparty out of reach, and the option to sell to the natural acquirer expires at the round that prices the company above what the acquirer can pay at all, a market capitalization smaller than the price, a wage cap, a fund's concentration limit, and past those a board's approval ceiling, with nobody at either table declining. The player's wage outgrows every club in the league but two. The practice is too large for any partner to buy in and too small to list. What goes is a counterparty, the buyer whose capacity was the option. What runs the clock is the acquirer's capacity, legible in its market value and its deal history, set against your own price, which each round raises. The move that would have kept it was the sale at the last price under the ceiling, which was never seen as the last, or a round sized to stay under it, which is the one choice a founder is never advised to make. This is analytical, since every observed case can be read as a buyer who would have paid more, so it stands as a mechanism and not as a count. The sign, then, is a number in the acquirer's filings, and the way to read it is against your own term sheet before you sign. Market-deaths' Slowed past the rot is a market that thins from the outside; this is the market for you that you thin by growing. It is not Chair grown over, where the counterparty re-plans; here the counterparty is unchanged and you have left its range.

The council vote is next week, and the sign is not on the agenda; it is in the ground. The new zoning will take the permission unless the building has substantially begun in reliance on a valid permit before the ordinance passes, and nothing on paper substitutes for that: not the permit, not the plans, not the letter. The footings are poured the week of the vote. The nonconforming use survives the new code only if it is in use on the effective date. The grandfathered rate is kept only by the account that was open. What goes is a permission. What runs the clock is the code and the vested-rights doctrine, which in most states vests on construction begun and in a few, Washington among them, on a complete application, so the last act differs by jurisdiction and the holder who knows which one applies has a different week than the holder who does not. The move that would have kept it is the hole in the ground before the vote, an exercise begun rather than a filing made; the option can be preserved only by starting to use it. So when the rule begins to move, read your own site for what has actually started. First-mover-forecloses holds the rival who changes the rules on purpose; this is the rule that changes for reasons of its own. It is not Slot flown empty, where the exercise must be repeated to keep the right; here one beginning vests it for good.

The aircraft is taking off with nobody aboard. That is not waste; it is the tell of a permission that expires by disuse and is kept only by exercise, so the clock runs while you do nothing and stops only when you act, and the act that keeps it is the exercise emptied of its purpose. The airport slot must be flown eighty percent of the season or returned, and in early 2020 airlines flew empty planes until the rule was waived. The water right under prior appropriation is forfeited after five years without beneficial use, so fields are irrigated in a drought to keep it. The trade mark is abandoned after three years' non-use. The mining claim is kept by annual labour. The department budget is spent in the last quarter so that it is not cut. What goes is a permission. What runs the clock is the regulator's usage ledger. The move that would have kept it is the empty flight, which costs the whole price of using the option and returns nothing but the option, so that keeping and using become one act and the option's upkeep is its exercise price. Watch the ledger, not the situation; the ledger is where the quiet accumulates. Runway-illusions' Stamp's clock is the licence that lapses without hours logged and that no cash extends; this is the price at which it can be extended after all, the hours flown for nobody. Tollgates-that-must-buy's Stamp with an expiry has the gate spending its stamp; here the permission-holder must burn the permission to keep it. Power-trades' Leased strike has disuse making a power unbelieved; here disuse forfeits it by rule. It is not Pour the foundation, one act that vests; here no act ever finishes the keeping.

The tray came out of the freezer this morning. Count what is on it against the bookings, because the count is the sign: whatever is not used by closing is gone, and it was not gone yesterday. Preparing to exercise the option starts a decay the unprepared state did not have, so the option to wait expires because the option to act was made ready. The vaccine vial keeps for months frozen, weeks once thawed, hours once punctured. The epoxy's pot life begins at mixing. The drawn dose, the armed fuze, the reagent brought to room temperature, the opened surgical field. The reserve army cannot be held at the frontier through the harvest it was drawn from. What goes is a capability, the good itself spoiling in its ready state. What runs the clock is a chemistry, or a season, that begins at preparation. The move that would have kept it is not preparing, or preparing in the smallest unit: the single-dose vial, the small mix, the tranche thawed for the day's bookings. The clinic that thaws a whole tray to be sure of serving whoever comes has bought its readiness with the doses it will discard at closing. This is the mirror of Slot flown empty, where the option dies of not being touched; here it dies of being touched, and a holder who holds both must burn the one and refrain from readying the other. It is not lead-time-floors' Understudy, a finished copy waiting, since the understudy does not spoil for having been rehearsed. And it is not Kept on the machine, where the harm falls on the holder and is billed by the day; here it falls on the good.

You are about to file your answer, and the small thing you are about to leave out of it is the only thing that matters. The objection to the court's jurisdiction over you is waived if it is not in the first response. The patent is dead in Europe on the morning of the conference talk, and dead in the United States a year after. The appeal is waived by accepting the settlement. The election of remedies. The defect in the goods must be objected to before the goods are used. Speak now, at the wedding, or hold your peace. The option must be taken before any other move on a linked matter, so its clock is your own next act rather than a date: do nothing and you keep it; do anything adjacent and it is gone. What goes is a permission. What runs the clock is a rule that binds the option to a position in a sequence, and the sequence is written somewhere other than the option, in the rules of procedure, the patent statute, the sales code, so most holders learn the order from the loss. The move that would have kept it is the ordering itself: the provisional filed the morning of the talk, the reservation written into the first filing, the objection lodged before the goods are unpacked, each costing nothing but the knowledge that an order exists. So before any first act, look for the rule that says what has to come first; the sign is that you have not looked. It is not Slot flown empty, where inaction runs the clock; here inaction is the only thing that keeps it. And it is not Bar date in the newspaper, since there is no date and you are the only one who can strike.

The new service is up, and the first record it writes will be in a shape the old schema cannot read. Nobody will decide anything about the rollback; the write will simply happen, in the ordinary course, and the way back will be gone. The option to reverse a move expires at the first act the new state performs that the old state cannot read, so the window is the pause between the change and its first consequence, and it closes without anyone closing it. The merger is reversible until the first combined payroll. The new address until the first piece of mail arrives there. The reorganization until the first hire into the new chart. The currency changeover until the first contract written in the new unit. What goes is a capability, the old state's ability to take over from here. What runs the clock is the first write, performed by the new state as routine and not as any decision about reversal. The move that would have kept it is the expand-and-contract shape, writing to both for a season so the old can still read, at the price of running two and of a season in which neither is the truth. So the sign is not an alarm; it is the first ordinary transaction, and you have to be watching for the ordinary. Pivot-invariants name the retained assets that make leaving cheap; this is the moment one of them is lost. Undo-costs bills a reversal that remains possible; this is the reversal that stops being possible. It is not Thawed to be ready, where readiness spoils the good; here the new state's use closes the way back to the old.

Week three on the circuit. The numbers that matter are not the ones on the monitor; they are the bleeding, the infection, the clotting, each a little higher than last week, and the centre's own written limit beyond which candidacy is reviewed. The patient on ECMO as a bridge to transplant is being kept alive by the thing that is, week by week, making her ineligible for the transplant it is bridging to. The mothballed mine is kept dry by pumps whose stopping floods the workings past reopening. The ship in the reserve fleet has its hull kept by cathodic protection that a budget line can end. The interim chief has run the company past the point where the search can bring in an outsider. The option is held open by a device or an upkeep whose own running accumulates a harm or whose lapse is one-way, so the deadline is the machine's and not the situation's. What goes is a capability, the eligibility or the workings. What runs the clock is the bridge itself, its complication rate or its upkeep bill. The move that would have kept it is the listing at the moment of cannulation, the search begun the day the interim was named, the decision to stop pumping taken while a sale was still possible, each of which treats the bridge's start as the option's deadline. The ECMO limits are centre practice and are simplified. So the sign is the day the bridge begins, and on that day the machine's clock is already running against the thing it holds open. Lead-time-floors' Bridge is a degraded replacement priced by the hour; this is the bridge that ends the option it holds open. It is not Standstill with a term, where the clock is a date the counterparty signs; here the clock is a harm nobody signs.

The tolling agreement runs twelve months, and it is month ten. Before you signed it there was no deadline in this situation; you wrote one in, to keep an option open, and the renewal of the paper belongs to the adversary, who now knows exactly what the pause is worth to you. That is the sign to read: a signature you need that is not yours. The tolling agreement stops a limitations clock you could have stopped alone by filing, and it expires unless the adversary signs again. The negotiated leave dates a job that had no date and is extended only if the employer signs. The forbearance holds the lender's foreclosure for ninety days. The furlough's recall rights run six months. The takeover standstill keeps the bidder from buying shares and ends on the day it says. What goes is a permission, the leave to remain in the paused state. What runs the clock is the pause's own instrument, the one clock in the situation you wrote yourself. The move that would have kept it is the renewal asked for before the counterparty learns it is needed, or a pause written without a term, which is rarely granted; the Korean armistice is the exception, with no renewal date and still called temporary. The statutory pauses, the family-leave statute's twelve weeks and the restraining order's fourteen days, are the same date without the mechanism, since the term is a rule's and the renewal belongs to a court or to no one, so the holder gets the deadline without paying the counterparty for it; those are runway-illusions' Stamp's clock. Impasse-inventions' cooling-off right offers reversibility as a chip; this is the bill the chip carries. It is not lead-time-floors' No-shop, which serializes the search; here the search is stopped, and the stopping is what expires.
